page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 64 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio of 4 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested systems with a stress-ng single-core score of 2674.77. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average tier, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 21390.8 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9335.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 1013.33 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 93.7 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets, including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, which contribute to an average Passmark CPU encryption score of 17158.62.

This instance offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads that require consistent CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized or compute-optimized tiers. The absence of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators makes it a cost-efficient choice for workloads relying on network-attached storage. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 13.61 GB/sec, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression tasks.
